name: James Lankford

issue_poll.name: Amber Integrated Oklahoma likely-voter survey, Oct 26–28, 2022; plus Pew Research Center national survey, Oct 10–16, 2022
issue_poll.note: Ranks 1–7 from Amber Integrated's Oklahoma most-important-issue question (economy/inflation 41%, preserving democracy 22%, education 10%, abortion 9%, illegal immigration 7%, health care 4%, crime 3%); 'preserving democracy' mapped to Elections / voting. Emerson (Oct 25–28) agrees on the top items but published only three. Ranks 8–10 from Pew's national 'very important' list (https://www.pewresearch.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/20/2022/10/PP_2022.10.20_midterms-economy_REPORT.pdf), skipping items already ranked: energy 61%, gun policy 57%, then foreign policy 54% (Supreme Court appointments, 55%, skipped because no vacancy arose this term).

issues.position: Oppose federalizing elections; keep election rules with states
issues.note: SAVE America Act sets federal voter-registration and ID rules; graded as for other senators who pledged against federalizing elections.

issues.position: Vote against federal funds that could promote critical race theory
issues.note: No Senate floor vote specifically on critical race theory funding this term.

issues.position: Block federal abortion-access bills; keep Hyde funding limits

votes.question: Cloture on the motion to proceed
Cloture on the motion to proceed

issues.position: Keep Title 42 border expulsions in place
issues.note: Title 42 ended May 2023 without a Senate floor vote on extending it.

issues.position: Roll back Medicare drug price negotiation

votes.question: On passage

issues.note: H.R.1 narrowed negotiation for orphan drugs; full repeal never got a floor vote.

Oppose red-flag laws and new gun limits

issues.note: Voted no in February because border provisions were dropped; voted yes on the April package.

caveats: Lankford held no general-election debate and his campaign site had no issue pages; positions come from campaign-year news and 2022 Senate releases.
Elections graded as contradicted: he pledged against federalizing elections, then voted to advance the SAVE America Act (he also led floor advocacy for it).
Health care rated on H.R.1's orphan-drug exemption, a partial rollback of negotiation; judgment call.
Roll call numbers for H.J.Res.44 and the Feb 13, 2024 H.R.815 passage vote were not confirmed for Lankford individually (party-line and news-reported votes).
